Essentials 2.0 · Flow inspiration · 10-dashboard

Dashboard: ideas from other products

This page looks at how other products build the first screen after login. That home must answer, for each role, what is happening, what needs me, and whether everything is working, then get people into the right module in one click. It covers role-based homes, today's agenda, center and room overview, system health, a few precise headline numbers and action items. It also covers customizable widgets (small boxes people can add to their home), module navigation, and the first-run setup guide. The full live room wall sits in Recording, the calendar in Scheduling, and full reports in Reports. Sources: the design reference libraries Mobbin and Refero, researched on 30 September 2026. All flows shown are from Mobbin, because Refero's image server refused every screenshot.

What we have today. Today's LearningSpace Essentials dashboard is a set of module tiles (Recording, Video Review, Reports, Scenario management, Calendar) plus a Center Overview of rooms and their calendar activity. The team itself calls it weak. The LearningSpace Enterprise facelift (mid-2026) was an accessibility and visual cleanup. It was redrawn, not rewritten: modules in their own row, a raised Upcoming tab, a Your Activities tab, buttons instead of links, and layouts that work on iPad and phone. A role-specific widget layer was deferred to phase 2. Essentials 2.0 aims for a central dashboard. It should combine learner feedback, faculty grading and reports, a system-health status fed by the automatic per-room device check, and a fast multi-room center overview. The rule is that a good dashboard shows little, but precisely. Whether to build it new or facelift the existing one is still open.

How to read this page

Each section below is one product. Each strip of screenshots is one flow: a real sequence of screens, in the order a user sees them. Click a screenshot to enlarge it. "Worth borrowing" lists ideas we could use, and "Avoid" lists what we should not copy. Use the task filters to see only one task, and click ☆ on a flow to add it to your own shortlist.

12 products · 21 flows · 88 screens · 9 tasks

What the best products have in common

  1. Health is shown on the list; the fix has an owner Google Home puts Offline on the room's device tile, so a problem is visible without opening it. Better Stack goes further: the home leads with the Ongoing incident and a sidebar count. Escalate names who was paged, Acknowledge records an owner, and Resolve closes it with a timeline. Google Home's fix path is only a help-article list plus Contact us. For Essentials, a failed room self-test should appear on the room in the overview. It becomes an owned item for the sim tech, who acknowledges, resolves, or escalates, then hands off to Recording for the device check.See: Google Home: Devices by room with an offline light · Better Stack: Escalate, acknowledge and resolve an incident · Google Home: Device detail to help and Contact us
  2. One dominant status, one main action Rivian's home is dominated by one number with one action pair under it, and everything else is smaller. Google Analytics is the opposite: many equal cards, each with its own controls, and no single answer. The dashboard's first line should be one verdict ('All rooms ready' or '2 rooms need attention') with one action, not a row of equally weighted widgets.See: Rivian: Vehicle home: one status, one action · Google Analytics: Analytics home with many equal cards
  3. A few headline numbers compared with the previous period; the detail lives in Reports Square's lean home shows five metrics under one location or date scope, with Reports in the sidebar. Each metric has a 'vs prior weekday' label that says N/A when there is no history. Fresha pairs two sales numbers with a 7-day trend. Patreon keeps one headline number with 'Go to Insights'. Square's own fuller home (nine metrics, banking promos, a near-empty chart) shows where it tips over. Three or four center headline numbers, each with the change since the last period and a link to Reports, is the most the evidence supports.See: Square: Lean home with key metrics · Fresha: Home: KPIs and today’s next appointments · Patreon: Switch from creator to member home · Square: Setup grid to full performance home
  4. Role homes are different jobs, and the current role is always named Patreon's switch rebuilds the whole home. The creator sidebar has management modules and Create. The member sidebar has five discovery items and no Create. The active role stays in the sidebar footer with a checkmark in the switcher. Aboard's admin home carries quick-create and approvals while the employee home carries personal first-time setup. Its switch is a one-way link with no role label afterwards. Coordinator, faculty, and learner homes should differ in content, not just hide menu items, and always show which role you are in.See: Patreon: Switch from creator to member home · Aboard: Admin home to employee portal
  5. Today is a short list by time, above the tasks Fresha lists today's next appointments with time, status (Booked/Started), staff, and duration. Notion groups Upcoming by day above My tasks, so the agenda and the to-dos share one scroll without a full calendar. Fresha's day grid has one column per staff member and a line marking the current time, which maps to one column per room. Neither puts the item's action on the row: Fresha shows status only, so 'Start recording' or 'Open debrief' on the agenda item has no reference here.See: Fresha: Home: KPIs and today’s next appointments · Notion: Home with upcoming events and my tasks · Fresha: Setup drawer, day grid and a no-show
  6. Action items: done, snooze, and read are different, and the count is precise Linear separates Done, Snooze, Mark all as read, and Delete all, counts unread only, and keeps snoozed items listed after the unread count reaches zero. Shopify and Aboard show countable work as one card ('2 orders to fulfill', '1 unhandled' time-off request) rather than a feed. Pending grading, recordings to share, and checklists to review fit this model, and each item opens Debrief, Recording, or Courses directly.See: Linear: Triage the inbox: done and snooze · Linear: Mark all as read vs. delete all · Shopify: Home · Aboard: Admin home to employee portal
  7. The setup guide lives on the home, follows you into the module, then leaves Shopify's guide is the home for a new store (N of M, one expanded task with its own button). It stays as a panel on the right while you do the task in the product editor, offers a sample product, and leaves via Dismiss guide and 'All caught up'. Fresha keeps setup progress in the header instead of taking the page. Better Stack shows the cost of not leaving: its checklist takes half the home while an incident is ongoing. A new center's checklist (rooms, cameras, users, first course) should hand off into Inventory, User management, and Courses, then get out of the way.See: Shopify: Home · Shopify: Using a setup guide · Fresha: Setup drawer, day grid and a no-show · Better Stack: Incidents home with setup checklist
  8. Admin-set defaults beat end-user widget building Jira's most useful piece is the Default dashboard that 'affects all users', with five layout presets. Its 31-gadget library, per-dashboard viewers and editors, and per-gadget controls are too much for non-technical faculty. Google Home keeps customisation to Reorder and Edit on Favourites. For the phase-2 widget layer, this points to per-role defaults set by the coordinator plus light show/hide or reorder, not a library.See: Jira: Edit the default dashboard layout · Jira: Create a dashboard and add gadgets · Google Home: Devices by room with an offline light

Questions we still need to answer

  • No product puts the item's action on the today row. Fresha's agenda shows status only. So 'Start recording', 'Open checklist', or 'Open debrief' from the session row has to be designed without a reference. The same goes for linking the two signals: what does the today row show when that session's room has failed its self-test?
  • Multi-room overview is still a gap. The nearest evidence is Google Home's room-grouped device tiles, Fresha's staff columns, and Square's locations table. No flow shows a free / in use / recording / problem strip for rooms. Security and room-booking apps (UniFi, Verkada, Robin, Skedda) returned nothing usable again. Refero was unusable because its image server blocked every screenshot.
  • What does 'all OK' look like? Better Stack shows health only through the presence of incidents. Rivian shows one metric. Should the dashboard show a green verdict with the last self-test time, or nothing until something fails? And who owns a failing room: is there a sim tech on duty to acknowledge it, as in Better Stack?
  • Role switching versus a merged home. Patreon switches identities. Aboard jumps one way to an employee portal. In a sim center one person is often both coordinator and faculty. Is that a switcher, or one home with both sets of sections? And does the learner need a dashboard at all, or only Patreon's member-style lightweight page with their own recordings and feedback?
  • Build new versus facelift. The sections with the strongest evidence (a today list fed by Scheduling, health on the rooms, an inbox with done/snooze, a first-run guide) are data-driven and new. The existing module tiles map to a short sidebar (Patreon, Notion). Can the LearningSpace Enterprise facelift shell host these sections, or is the tile row itself what has to go?
  • Multi-campus is only a pointer. Square's location filter and Google Home's home switcher switch one scope at a time and say nothing about access across separate LearningSpace instances.

Fresha

Close match2 flows

Fresha is the closest match to a sim coordinator's day. Its home shows two sales headline numbers and a 7-day trend above today's next appointments (time, status, staff). It also has a day grid with one column per staff member and a line marking the current time, which could work with one column per room. Its agenda rows show status only, with no Start action.

WebOther6 steps

Home: KPIs and today’s next appointments

moves from an empty day calendar into the Home dashboard. They scan sales and appointment headline numbers and activity, then scroll to today's next appointments plus this-month-versus-last-month service and team tables.

Today and upcomingA few precise headline numbersEmpty screen and setup guideModule navigation and quick actions

Worth borrowing

  • Today's next appointments list shows time, BOOKED or STARTED status, client, duration, and staff (screens 2-6), so the dashboard agenda hands off into Scheduling.
  • The recent sales card shows a big number, appointment count and value, and a dual trend line for the last 7 days (screens 2-4).
  • When the schedule is empty, the upcoming card says so honestly instead of showing fake charts (screen 2).
  • Header 'Complete Setup' progress (60% to 100%) stays visible on Home (screens 1-6) without owning the whole page.

Avoid

  • Today's rows show status only, with no Start, Check-in, or Open session control on the card (screens 2-6). Essentials still needs a direct jump into Recording or Debrief from the agenda item.

What it means for Essentials Dashboard: replaces a weak tile-only home with a compact headline-number strip and today's agenda that clicks through into Scheduling, and later Recording or Debrief. Report tables hand off into Reports, not a second Reports home.

Better Stack

Same task, different field2 flows

Better Stack shows the failing case properly. The home leads with an Ongoing incident and a sidebar count, then Escalate (naming who was paged), Acknowledge (recording who owns it), and Resolve with a timeline. It shows no 'all OK' summary at all.

WebOther4 steps

Escalate, acknowledge and resolve an incident

opens an Ongoing unacknowledged incident, acknowledges it so the owner is shown, resolves it with an AI post-mortem, then reviews details and a timeline of acknowledge and resolve.

System health at a glanceAction items and notifications

Worth borrowing

  • The problem state offers Escalate and Acknowledge, and a green banner names who was escalated to (Alex), so who to call is explicit.
  • Acknowledge stamps the owner, and the main button flips to Resolve (screen 2).
  • Resolve closes the loop with duration, severity, team, and owner details, plus a timestamped timeline, as a guided ownership path rather than a help-article list.
  • These screens convey health by incident presence and sidebar count, without an at-a-glance All OK view.

What it means for Essentials Dashboard: Acknowledge then Resolve with a named owner is the system-health fix path for failed room self-tests. Deep device repair still hands off to Recording, while Who's on-call maps to User management and the sim-tech roster.

Google Home

Outside idea2 flows

Google Home groups devices under room headers and shows Offline on the tile itself, so a problem room is visible without opening it. Its fix path is a generic help list plus Contact us, which is the weak version to improve on.

iOSOther4 steps

Devices by room with an offline light

opens the Favourites home, then the Devices list where rooms group device tiles and an Offline light is visible without opening a device. Later the same list shows devices online.

Center overview and room statusSystem health at a glanceCustomizable widgets

Worth borrowing

  • Offline shows on the room tile itself as a gray card with an Offline label and warning triangle. You do not need to open it to see the problem.
  • Devices are grouped under room headers (Living room) with status on the tile (On at 100% versus Offline) (screens 2-3).
  • Favourites Reorder and Edit are explicit entry points to rearrange widgets (screen 1).
  • A home location switcher sits in the header for multi-site centers (screens 1-3).

Avoid

  • Screens 3 and 4 are a duplicate all-online Devices capture. Do not treat the repeat as a distinct change.

What it means for Essentials Dashboard: room-grouped device tiles with Offline on the list extend Center Overview and hand off problem rooms to Recording for audio and video (AV) and device check. Favourites Reorder and Edit are dashboard-only widgets, not a replacement for module tiles.

  • A gamified 'unlock a rare accessory' trial pop-up is noise for a clinical ops dashboard (screen 2).

What it means for Essentials Dashboard: sidebar pattern for Essentials module navigation (Recording, Scheduling, Reports, and so on) plus a dashboard-only Welcome checklist. Companion-app links resemble handoffs to Calendar or Scheduling rather than widgets.

Customizable widgetsA few precise headline numbersModule navigation and quick actions

Worth borrowing

  • An empty Insights illustration when nothing to recommend withholds extra chrome until there is a finding (screen 3).

Avoid

  • Many equal-weight cards (headline-number tabs, realtime, suggestions, each with its own dropdowns and links) and no single primary answer (screens 1-3) raise scan time. The user cannot tell where to look first or what 'OK' means.

What it means for Essentials Dashboard: clutter example to avoid. Do not build an Essentials dashboard like this. It conflicts with show little, precisely. Headline numbers and deep charts belong in Reports, not as competing hero widgets on the home.
